purpose: set the direction that product and engineering work will serve, in terms the organization can test and fund
entry_criteria: Business context and leadership input are available
Market and financial data can be gathered
A sponsor is accountable for the strategy
procedure: State the business goals and the time horizon in measurable terms.
Describe the market position, customers served and what makes the offering different, using evidence.
Assess strengths, gaps and constraints in people, technology and money.
Set a small number of strategic choices, including what not to do, with reasons.
Turn each choice into outcomes and measures that product teams can plan against.
Review on a schedule and revise when evidence changes, recording what changed and why.
acceptance_criteria: Choices include what is not pursued
A review date and owner exist

validation.check: check every strategic goal has a measure, an owner and a date
trace each claim about the market to a cited source
validation.expect: all traced or marked as assumption

failure_modes.response: Label them and plan to test

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A company sets a goal of 20 percent more recurring revenue in two years by focusing on mid-sized customers and deliberately not building a consumer product, with quarterly review of three measures.
